citation.authors: Aygun B, Lane A, Smart LR et al

cited_by.title: Sickle cell disease: what it is, treatment and newborn screening

record.population: 606 children aged 1 to 10 with haemoglobin SS or S-beta-zero thalassaemia given hydroxyurea in Kenya, Uganda, Angola and the Democratic Republic of Congo (635 enrolled)
record.design: Open-label, non-randomised phase 1/2 trial (REACH) with up to 8 years of follow-up
record.finding: Escalating hydroxyurea under monitoring to the maximum tolerated dose reduced pain episodes (rate ratio 0.60 against the fixed-dose phase), acute chest syndrome (0.21), malaria (0.58) and non-malarial infections (0.52), and raised haemoglobin from 7.3 to 8.5 g/dL; serious side effects were uncommon. The abstract gave no significant change in deaths (0.70, P 0.50).
record.note: Uncontrolled: it compares dosing phases within the same children, not against placebo. Participants were selected by haemoglobin genotype.
